I don't have any notes for you yet. My only attempt to fetch sources (Enduring Word, Gill on StudyLight, Ellicott on BibleHub, Precept Austin and the NET Bible notes on Psalm 139) failed because of a bug in my processing code. The tool then hit its usage limit for this turn, so I couldn't fix the bug or read any other pages.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. Since I didn't read anything, I can't make any verified points about any verse, any differences between traditions, or any other views. I won't fill the gaps from memory.

**What I'll do when you ask me to continue:**
1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word (Guzik), Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary and Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (on BibleHub or StudyLight), plus Precept Austin.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Verses 13–16 are a likely example, covering when life begins, whether "written in Your book" means God's decree or his foreknowledge, and how the soul originates. Verses 19–22, on "perfect hatred," are another. For these I'll use Reformed sources (Ligonier, TGC, Monergism), Baptist sources (Desiring God, GTY, Spurgeon.org), Wesleyan sources (Wesley's notes at wesley.nnu.edu, Seedbed) and Lutheran sources (LCMS, 1517).
3. **Other views:** The NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for verse 15 ("depths of the earth"), verse 16 ("unformed body") and the textual problems in verse 20. Augustine and the Church Fathers on New Advent, plus Catholic.com and OCA, for verses 13–16 and verses 21–22.

Just reply "continue" and I'll start fetching those pages.
